items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And also, my friend Frank Cuomo, who I went to school with at the New York Conservatory of Modern Music

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, the big orchestral piece.

With a big orchestra. And so the contractor had contacted a friend of mine, a French horn player, Les Ellman, who was responsible for me playing shows and things like that. And also, my friend Frank Cuomo, who I went to school with at the New York Conservatory of Modern Music, in terms of copying, were also professional copyists and orchestrators and all of that. So in dealing with that beforehand, that’s when he had his place on Prince Street. And so what happened, for the rehearsal Les asked me to bring the…

it in England. And I’ve still got the bassoon part. So that was actually my experience with him, which was a great experience to see him handle all this and deal with it. And then finally to get a copy of the recording and see how it came out. And how are you going to beat the BBC?
